notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 2 continuous 22.5-ft bays, W24X117 girders, one 15-ton pendant crane, on new freestanding W14X211 columns with built-up tapered I haunches, base plates, anchor rods and spread footings, and crane-level rod X-bracing; the existing building carries no crane load. Seismic: ordinary steel cantilever column system across the runway and rod bracing not specifically detailed for seismic resistance along it, Seismic Design Category B. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier. The bracket stays: the W10X60 crane-level strut is moment-connected in plan at every column by 0.5 in plates on its flanges (torsion brace, 2 rows of bolt pairs) and holds the new W14X211 columns against the twist: 0.0060 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 0.143 in of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 0.665 in). With the strut on the column centerline alone, the girder seated 37.85 in off the column axis, the traction twists the column 0.1319 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 3.119 in of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 0.665 in). The strut is sized so the girder's twist movement under the factored traction stays within 0.125 in (a configurator target, the TR-13 alignment tolerance class, so the tie, slots and gaps are not sized by it).

selections.reason: The support reaction, about 53 kip, is above the AIST TR-13 §5.9.2 guideline of 50 kip for column brackets, a clause to be verified: consider column caps over the new columns; an advisory, not a code limit, so the support entered (Built-up tapered I haunch) is kept and checked here.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): H1 top-flange interaction with the load-height LTB strength ratio 0.75, vertical deflection 0.25 and lateral 0.41 of their limits; flanges at least 10.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 10 by sizing ratio, 62 by flange width; the next lighter, W30X116: tips ratio 1.12 > 0.85. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios.
New cantilever column for a 15-ton crane (W14X120 to 5 t, W14X159 to 12.5 t, W14X211 to 25 t, else W14X257).
Set by the tie sizing: the column face moves out from 20 in (to at most 30 in) until the tie passes its imposed-movement and strength checks.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints tight (gap 1/16 in max.), supplier's joint bars (deferred submittal) installed slip-critical: Class A surfaces, bolts pretensioned, re-tightened at 30 and 90 days.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
